newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Burundi army censured for killing civilians.
newsitem.headline: Burundi army censured for killing civilians.

text.p: The Burundi defence ministry has ordered the arrest of an army officer after an army unit was held responsible for clashes in which 79 civilians died earlier this month, a spokesman in Bujumbura said on Thursday.

The army spokesman, in an apparently unprecedented admission of army responsibility, told reporters that most of those killed during fighting between the army and armed Hutu rebels in the clashes in Kizuka, southern Burundi, were civilians.
He did not specify whether the civilians were knowingly killed by troops or died in the cross-fire or because of mistaken identity. The army usually blames all civilian deaths on the rebels.
The spokesman said the fighting in Rumonga commune began on December 16 when rebels attacked a camp for displaced Hutus at Kizuka, killing 12.
When the Burundi army intervened, another 67 people, mostly civilians, were killed.

Last week, allegations by the humanitarian organisation Amnesty International that more than a thousand civilians had been killed by the Burundi army in the past month were rejected by the Burundi government.
Diplomats said it appeared that the pressure of international opinion was forcing the Burundi authorities to take action to control its Tutsi-led armed forces.
